mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Internal HTTP policy

The project's current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception: internal hosts are held to the same standard as any other host, on the basis that proper certificate management is now in place.

cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. Its paragraph says the current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception for internal hosts, because certificate management is now in place.

Muninn holds two conflicting statements on this. An earlier one said plain HTTP was fine for internal hosts because they sit behind the firewall. A later one, recorded seconds afterward, says "https everywhere, no plaintext exception", and the assistant's reply then read it as replacing the earlier note. I used the later one and left the retired exception out of the file, as you asked.

Both are trust-1 episode excerpts, not formal decision records, so nothing catalogued as a decision covers this. If you want a firmer basis, confirm the HTTPS-everywhere policy explicitly so it gets recorded as a decision.

The first attempt to create the file through the shell failed with a parser error, so I wrote it with the file tool instead.
